_: Kinds of security product for AI agents, each written as the answers it can change in the RiskGraph model. These are RiskMandate's reading of what the category does, not any vendor's claim; a named case replaces a row's reading with the vendor's own words. Each row's baseline is the model's typical deployment with the questions it changes answered as they would be without it. Examples are names and documentation links only, read 24 September 2026, in no order.
intro: Twelve kinds of product that could sit around an agent, each computed against the typical deployment with its own questions answered as they would be without it. Every row is our reading of what the category does, not any vendor’s claim, and the change is conservative on purpose: where a category could move an answer to *partly* or *fully*, the row says *partly*.
note: Two patterns are worth reading off the table. Most categories retire one or two entries each, so the case for any single product is narrow and exact rather than broad, and a register gets small by combining them. And every category adds something: a service in the request path, a store of prompts, a credential with wide reach. The case is only honest with that column in it.

items.name: AI gateways and egress proxies
items.what: Between the agent and model providers or the internet: routing, limiting and logging outbound calls.
items.adds_text: Another service in the request path; provider keys held in one place; a log store holding prompts and data.

items.name: MCP gateways
items.what: In front of MCP tool servers: filtering, authorising and logging tool calls.
items.adds_text: In the request path; holds credentials for many tool servers; a log of every tool call.

items.name: Agent identity and non-human identity
items.what: Each agent its own identity, with an owner, delegation, and a record of the tokens it is issued.
items.adds_text: The identity provider becomes a dependency for every token; stored third-party tokens; delegated access that stays open.

items.name: Sandboxes and isolated execution
items.what: Short-lived, isolated compute for the code an agent runs.
items.adds_text: Often a hosted runtime, so code and data go to the vendor; new API keys; an escape surface.

items.name: Runtime monitoring and tracing
items.what: Traces of prompts, tool calls and outputs, so what the agent did can be read back.
items.adds_text: A telemetry store holding prompts and personal data; an SDK inside the agent; often a hosted processor.

items.name: Policy engines, policy as code
items.what: Allow and deny decisions made outside the agent's own code, per action.
items.adds_text: A decision point in the path; a fail-open or fail-closed choice somebody has to make; policy distribution.

items.name: Human approval layers
items.what: An action waits until a named person approves it.
items.adds_text: The notification channel becomes attack surface; a dependency on the approval service; what happens at timeout.

items.name: Data masking and DLP for AI
items.what: Personal or special-category data detected and redacted before the model or its tools see it.
items.adds_text: The inspecting service sees everything in the clear; in the path; what it misses is not measured.

items.name: Backup and point-in-time restore
items.what: Snapshots of the data and configuration an agent changes, and a way to put them back.
items.adds_text: A second full copy of the data; a backup credential with wide read access. Anything changed since the last snapshot is still lost, which is why the row says partly.

items.name: Kill switches and agent control planes
items.what: A runtime switch that turns an agent or one of its capabilities off without a redeploy.
items.adds_text: The switch's own service is a dependency, and what its client does when that service is unreachable decides whether it fails open or closed. Having a switch is not having used one: whether it was ever pulled in production stays unanswered.

items.name: Browser isolation for agents
items.what: Remote, disposable browsers for agents that browse the web.
items.adds_text: The vendor sees page content and logged-in sessions; stored cookies and browser contexts.

items.name: AI security posture management
items.what: Finds agents, models and their permissions across cloud accounts.
items.adds_text: Read access across the cloud estate; a new inventory of sensitive findings. Like a behaviour policy, it mostly turns an unknown into an answer rather than changing the exposure.

items.name: Host-level agent inventory and stop
items.what: On the machine itself: which agents are running, what each can reach and has connected to, and a way to stop one, for the account the tool runs as.
items.adds_text: A report on disk that describes the host; an optional capture helper holding a raw-socket capability; a sensor the agent's own account can stop.

items.name: Agent harnesses and runtimes
items.what: Around the agent: the session, the sandbox it runs in, the approvals that pause it, and the log of every step, held by an operator rather than by the agent.
items.adds_text: A control plane holding prompts, repository content and the log; the harness's own components; an approval that is a person clicking.
